# minino

> Electronic Cats Minino — 802.15.4 and Zigbee analysis board

**Vendor:** Electronic Cats  ·  **class:** [badgelife](badgelife-class.md)

Status: **supported** — the identifiers and setup recipe are believed correct.

**Maintainer-verified** 2026-08-26 on Pop!_OS 22.04: Attached and enumerated; identifier, product string and serial captured with scripts/identify-device.sh. The radio side was not exercised and no firmware was flashed.

## What it is

A compact ESP32-based board aimed at IEEE 802.15.4 and Zigbee work, from the same maker as CatSniffer.

## What you can do with it

Capture and inspect 802.15.4 and Zigbee traffic, and run alternative firmware for specific tasks.

## Setup

Flash with esptool and open a console with tio — the badgelife class this device joins provides both. Add yourself to dialout and plugdev, then log out and back in.

## Known problems

Capture behaviour depends on which firmware variant is loaded. The USB identifier is confirmed by capture (303a:1001) — the shared ESP32-S3 USB-JTAG identifier, which is why it is carried as ambiguous rather than as a symlink source.

## How it identifies itself

| USB id | What | Confirmed | Node |
|---|---|---|---|
| `303a:1001` | Espressif ESP32-S3 native USB JTAG/serial peripheral | yes | serial |

**⚠ `303a:1001` is not unique to this device** (vendor_chip_default; also used by: clip-boy, free-wili-2, every ESP32-S3 or ESP32-C3 board using native USB). esptool calls 0x1001 USB_JTAG_SERIAL_PID, a constant of the ESP32-S3/C3 USB-serial-JTAG peripheral. Confirmed by three captures of three unrelated products -- this board, clip-boy, and the ESP32-S3 inside free-wili-2 -- all reporting the identical pair AND the identical product string. Only the serial differs, and a serial is per-unit.

## Access and permissions

Group membership required: `dialout`, `plugdev` — added at install, applies at next login.
